newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: VIRGIN ATLANTIC LINKS WITH S.AFRICA'S SUN AIR.
newsitem.headline: VIRGIN ATLANTIC LINKS WITH S.AFRICA'S SUN AIR.

text.p: Virgin Atlantic Airways has signed a code-sharing agreement with Sun Air, an airline earmarked by the South African government for privatisation, the local carrier announced on Sunday.
A Sun Air statement said the companies would coordinate their schedules to offer Virgin's long-haul passengers connection from Johannesburg to the key tourist destinations of Cape Ticaand Durban.

"(Sun Air) has been identified by Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau as a candidate for early privatisation, but Virgin Atlantic currently has no plans to invest equity as part of the code-share agreement," the statement said.
It quoted Virgin's Richard Branson as saying the deal might also "lead to further connections as Sun Air expands its operation in southern Africa".
Sun Air's managing director Johan Borstlap said the code-sharing agreement would lead to special air fares, but he did not elaborate.
Virgin is to start direct Johannesburg-to-London flights on October 3, starting with three flights a week and increasing to six next year. The company also hopes to launch package holidays in 1997.
South Africa's largest independent carrier, Comair, signed a franchise agreement with British Airways Plc in June under which its aircraft will use the BA name and livery.
